title: We used AI to build a playable horror game in one week. Here's what broke
author: marcovice
selftext:
Hi! I'm Lia, one half of a 2-person team. We're making our very first game, a narrative horror game in Unity for GitHub Game Off 2026. My partner builds it with Claude Code, and in the first week we had it playable from start to finish (in grey boxes).

The idea: most horror games scare you with ghosts. Ours has zero. You play a night-shift pharmacist with some secrets, and the scary part is getting caught. Every choice leaves a trace, and someone is going to check.

Things that broke in week one:  
Our CCTV looked horribly blurry. We blamed the camera for a whole day. It was the road. The road was too shiny.  
A customer kept vanishing right in front of the counter. Like a ghost. In our no-ghost game. Now they walk away first and disappear where you can't see.  
My teammate texted me "the game is gone." Unity had just opened the wrong, empty scene. Best horror moment of the week.

Next up: making it look like an old PS1 game.  
Question for you: what scares you more, a ghost or getting caught?
